abhikīrati:
abhikirati
abhikīrati1 (mc pr. 3 sg. [S. abhikirati], scatters; pours (itself) over; overwhelms; S I 54,21* (kacci tam ekam āsīnaṃ aratī nābhikīrati); Dhp 25 (dīpaṃ … yaṃ ogho nābhikīrati; Dhp-a I 255,.18 : yaṃ … kilesogho ~ituṃ viddhaṃsetuṃ na sakkoti); Ja III 57,23* (kiṃ vo sokagaṇābhikīrare; 58,8´ : kiṃkāraṇā tumhe sokarāsī ~anti ajjhottharanti); IV 121,3* (dīpaṃ … yaṃ jarā nābhikīrati; 121,6´ : yaṃ jarā nābhikīrati na viddhaṃseti); VI 541,25* (nandiyo mābhikīrare; 541,28´ : maṃ somanassāni abhikīranti abhikkamanti); Mil 181,.6 ([rajo] yena vā tena vā ~ati); — pass. 3 sg. abhikīrati2, is scattered, is dispersed; Th 598 (saññā me abhikīranti vivekapaṭisaṃyutā, Ce, Ee, Se so; Be abhikiranti; cf Th-a II 256,.21 : me cittaṃ vivekapaṭisaṃyutā saññā abhikiranti vivekatṭhānaṃ yeva ākaḍḍhanti, Be, Ce, Se so; Ee abhikīranti); —     pp     abhikiṇṇa,   mfn., strewn with, covered with; overwhelmed by; Mp II 126,.27 (sakalavihāro missakapupphehi ~o viya ahosi); Vv-a 38,.15 (pupphābhikiṇṇan ti pupphehi ~aṃ); — ifc see dukkhâ-, pupphâ-.
bhabba:
1bhabba
mfn. [from bhabbati], injuring;? Sadd 405,.12 (bhabba hiṃsāyaṃ: bhabbati ~o).

2bhabba
bhavya mfn. 1. [BHS bhavya] (i) able (to), capable (of); competent; fit for, with the potential for; (usually + dat. or inf.); Abh 1071 (~aṃ yogge); Vin I 17,.18 (~o nu kho Yaso gahapati hīnāyāvattitvā kāme paribhuñjtuṃ seyyathā pi pubbe agārikabhūto ti); II 254,.29 (~o nu kho bhante mātugāmo tathāgatappavedite dhammavinaye … pabbajitvā sotāpattiphalaṃ vā … arahattaṃ vā sacchikātun ti); V 117,.16 (dve puggalā ~ā āpattiṃ āpajjituṃ bhikkhū ca bhikkhuniyo ca); M I 104,.1 foll. (bhikkhu … ~o sambodhāya ~o anuttarassa yogakkhemassa adhigamāya); 222,.20 (ekādasahi bhikkhave aṅgehi samannāgato gopālako ~o gogaṇaṃ pariharituṃ) ≠ A V 350,.25; S II 196,.1 (ātāpī ca kho ottāpī ~o sambodhāya ~o nibbānāya); A III 75,13* (nāhaṃ ~o etarahi kāmāni paṭisevituṃ); V 147,.9 (tayo … dhamme pahāya ~o jātiṃ pahātuṃ jaraṃ pahātuṃ maraṇaṃ pahātuṃ); Ud 49,.2 (ko nu kho idha ~o dhammaṃ viññātun ti; Ud-a 281,.8 foll.: maggaphaladhammaṃ adhigantuṃ samattho); It 106,19* (~ā te antakiriyāya); It-a I 106,.10 (°-taṃ dassento); — (ii) fit for, capable of, with the potential for, spiritual progress; Vibh 342,.1 (katame te sattā ~ā); Mil 167,.11 (ye te sattā ~ā te dhammāmatena bujjhanti ye pana te sattā abhabbā te dhammāmatena haññanti patanti); Vism 116,.13 (thero ~ā vat’ ime bhikkhū ti kammaṭṭhānaṃ kathesi); Nidd-a I 298,.26 foll. (ariyāya jātiyā bhavanti jāyantī ti ~ā, vattamānasamīpe vattamānavacanaṃ, bhavissanti jāyissanti vā ti ~ā … ye ariyamaggapaṭivedhassa anucchavikā upanissayasampannā te ~ā, vuttapaṭipakkhā abhabbā); — 2. [cf S. bhavya, bhāvya], about to be, likely to be, future; just existing, developing; what ought to be, proper, good; see R.M.L. Gethin, 2015; Abh 1071 (~aṃ … bhāvini); M III 215,.17 foll. (atthi kammaṃ ~aṃ c’ eva bhabbābhāsaṃ ca, atthi kammaṃ ~aṃ abhabbābhāsan ti; Ps V 20,.5 foll.; Ps-ṭ [Be] IV 380,.27 : bhavati vaḍḍhati etenā ti ~aṃ, vaḍḍhinimittaṃ); Ja V 325,10´ (bhavyāni ca taruṇadevatāni); VI 155,7´ (vaḍḍhitvā ṭhitā sattasaṅkhātā bhūtā ca idāni vaḍḍhanakasattasaṅkhātāni bhavyāni ca); Sv 112,.4 foll. (ahaṃ pitā bhūtānaṃ ca bhavyānaṃ cā ti … aṇḍajajalābujā sattā anto aṇḍakose … bhavyā nāma bahi nikkhantakālato paṭṭhāya bhūtā nāma); Sadd 847,.25 (bhavitabbo ~o bhavitabbaṃ ~aṃ); — ifc see bhūta- (sv bhavati); — bhavyaṃ in Ee at A II 44,4* is prob. wr; Be habyaṃ; Ce hutaṃ; Se huññaṃ; —      °’-āpattika, mfn., capable of committing an offence; Vin V 115,.22; Sp 1320,.26 (sāvakā ~ā nāma); —       ° âbhabbakā, m.f.pl., (those) who are capable and not capable (of progress); Bv-a 91,.35; —       °-rūpa, mfn., [cf S. bhavyarūpa], having a good or suitable appearance; seeming very capable; A I 189,.11 (mā anussavena … mā ~-tāya, Be, Ce, Se so; Ee bhavya-; Mp II 305,.27 foll.: ayaṃ bhikkhu ~o, imassa kathaṃ gahetuṃ yuttan ti pi mā gaṇhittha); Ud 79,24* (mohasambandhano loko ~o va dissati; cf Ud-a 386,.5 : yo idha sattaloko ~o va hetusampanno viya hutvā dissati) quoted Nett 62,.8 (62,.13 : viparītapaññatti lokassa); Sp 967,.24 (~o hoti sahetuko ñāto yasassī kulaputto); Spk I 298,.23 (tasmiṃ pana attabhāve maggaphalānaṃ ~ā puggalā); —     abhabba, mfn., 1. not able, not capable; not fit for; not capable of spiritual progress; Vin I 17,.6; V 117,.15 (dve puggalā ~ā āpattiṃ āpajjituṃ buddhā ca paccekabuddhā ca); D III 13,.23 (~o kho … acelo Pāṭikaputto taṃ vācaṃ appahāya … mama sammukhībhāvaṃ āgantuṃ); 133,.14 foll. (~o āvuso khīṇāsavo bhikkhu sañcicca pāṇaṃ jīvitā voropetuṃ); M I 464,.29 (tālo matthakacchinno ~o puna virūḷhiyā); S III 27,.2 (rūpaṃ … appajahaṃ ~o dukkhakkhayāya); Dhp 32 (~o parihānaya); It 117,20* (~o tādiso bhikkhu phuṭṭhuṃ sambodhim uttamaṃ); Sn 232 (~-tā diṭṭhapadassa vuttā); Ja VI 70,.1 (~o bhavissāmi kiṃ me pabbajjāya); Vibh 341,.37 (katame te sattā ~ā); Vism 54,.16 (~o visesādhigame); 388,.6 (atha naṃ thero ~o tvaṃ sāsane ti vihārato nīhari); Sp 1209,.15 (~o c’ esa puttapaṭilābhassa); Sv 739,.23 (~-ttā); — ~’-āpattika, mfn., not capable of committing an offence; Vin V 115,.22; Sp 1320,.27 (buddhā ca paccekabuddhā ca ~’-āpattikā nāma); — ~’-uppattika, mfn., not capable of arising (again); Ja II 327,10´ (taṃ purisaṃ … puna tāya sampattiyā ~’-uppattikaṃ kurumānā, Be, Se so; Ce, Ee abhāvuppattiṃ); Nidd I 53,.28 (eso gedho pahīno … ~-uppattiko; Nidd-a I 171,.4 foll.: puna uppajjituṃ abhabbo); Dhp-a I 283,.3; — 2. not proper, not good; M III 215,.15 foll. (atthi kammaṃ ~aṃ abhabbābhāsaṃ atthi kammaṃ abhabbaṃ bhabbābhāsaṃ).
bhuja:

m.n. 2bhuja
mfn. [S. bhuj], possessing; ruling; — ifc see bhū- (sv bhū1).
esana:
2esana
mfn. [S. eṣaṇa], seeking, searching for; S I 61,10* (sukhajīvino pure āsuṃ bhikkhū Gotamasāvakā anicchā piṇḍam ~ā, eds so, perhaps wr for esānā).
khipanaka:
1khipanaka
mfn. [khipana1 + ka2], who throws, who tosses; Vism 489,.29 (aṅgārakāsuyaṃ °-purisā, Be, Ce, Ee so; Se khipana-) ≠ Vibh-a 80,.30 (°-puriso, Be so; Ce, Ee, Se khipana-).

2khipanaka
n. [from khipati2], sneezing; Thūp 179,.21 (yakkhagāhakakhipanaka-arocake karissāmi) ≠ Sv 610,.26 (Ce -khipitaka-ārocake; Be yakkhagāhakhipitaka-arocake; Ee yakkhagāhakhipana-ārocanake; Se yakkhagāha-khipanaka-ābādhike; Sv-pṭ II 245,.14 : ~aṃ … khipitakarogo, Ee so; Be khipitakan ti).
ādāya:
2ādāya
m. [from ādiyati1], (the adopting of) a belief, a view; Vin I 70,.20 (tassa satthuno tassa diṭṭhiyā tassa khantiyā tassa ruciyā tassa ~assa avaṇṇe bhaññamāne; Sp 993,.8 : sā yeva laddhi yasmā … daḷhagāhena gahitā tasmā … ~o ti vuccati); 355,.26 (tesaṃ diṭṭhiṃ ca khantiṃ ca ruciṃ ca ~aṃ ca rocehi); 359,19* (sakaṃ ca ~am ayaṃ na riñcati; Sp 1154,.1 : sakaṃ ~aṃ attano ācariyavādaṃ na hāpeti); Vibh 245,.28 (idhā ti imissā diṭṭhiyā imissā khantiyā imissā ruciyā imasmiṃ ~e imasmiṃ dhamme imasmiṃ vinaye).

3ādāya
ind. [absol. of ā2 + √dā3; cf S. ādyati], fastening to; having fixed (on); Ja IV 272,22* (ādāya pattiṃ … cāpe saraṃ; 272,28´ : saraṃ cāpe ādāya sannayhitvā).
ānantariya:
1ānantarika
ānantariya1 mfn. and n. [from anantara; BHS ānantarya], 1. (mfn.) immediately preceding or following, next; nearest; Vin I 321,.26 (antamaso ~assāpi bhikkhuno, Be, Ce, Ee so; Se anantarikassāpi; Sp 1147,.6 : ~assā ti attano anantaraṃ nisinnassa, Be so; Ce, Ee, Se anantarikassā ti); II 165,.5 (~aṃ bhikkhuṃ vuṭṭhāpesi, Be, Ce so; Ee, Se anantarikaṃ); 212,.35 (~aṃ bhikkhuṃ āpucchitvā, Be, Ce, Ee so; Se anantarikaṃ); Sadd 319,.34 (dvinnaṃ h’ ettha suddhassarānaṃ anantarikānaṃ ekato sannipāto anupapatti); — 2. (mfn.) immediate; bringing immediate results; (of an action) producing consequences in the immediately following existence; (of a person) suffering immediate retribution, suffering consequences in the immediately following existence; (n.) an action producing consequences in the immediately following existence; Vin V 128,.25 (pañca kammāni ~āni); D III 273,.7 (~o cetosamādhi, Be, Ce, Ee so; Se anantariko); Sn 226 (samādhiṃ ~aṃ yam āhu); Ja I 45,5* (muttā ~ehi, Be, Ce, Se so; Ee ānantarīkehi); Dhs 1028 (pañca kammāni ~āni, Be, Ce, Se so; Ee anantarikāni; As 358,.18 : ~ānī ti anantarāyena phaladāyakāni, mātughātakammādīnaṃ etaṃ adhivacanaṃ); Pp 13,.20 (pañca puggalā ~ā); Kv 365,.15 (~assa puggalassa n’ atthi antarābhavo ti); 593,.2 (asañcicca mātaraṃ jīvitā voropetvā ~o hotī ti); Sp 452,.28 (sace mātāpitaro maranti ānantariyaṃ pi hoti); 1023,.6 (tassa pabbajjā na vāritā na ca ānantariyo hoti); Mp II 5,.7 (mātaraṃ vā pitaraṃ vā … jīvitā voropentassa kammaṃ ~iyaṃ hoti); 211,.20 (pañcannaṃ pi ānantariyānaṃ kattā); Vin-vn 295 (ānantariyavatthusmiṃ ānantariyam eva ca); 322 (pañc’ ~ā); Utt-vn 689 (tasmānantariyaṃ n’ atthi māritesu ubhosu pi); —      °-kamma,   n., an action bringing retribution in the immediately following existence; Vin II 193,.37 (idaṃ bhikkhave Devadattena paṭhamaṃ ~aṃ upacitaṃ); Mp II 27,.16 foll. (pañca hi ānantariyakammāni mahāsāvajjāni nāma); — see also anantarika, ānantariya2.

2ānantariya

[S. ānantarya], immediacy, immediate sequence or succession; the state bringing immediate results; A II 149,.28 (~aṃ pāpuṇāti āsavānaṃ khayāya; Mp III 138,.13 : ~an ti anantaravipākadāyakaṃ maggasamādhiṃ; cf Sn 226: samādhiṃ ānantarikaṃ yam āhu) quoted Vism 675,.19 (eds ānantarikaṃ); Paṭis-a 99,.3 (nāssa antaraṃ atthī ti anantaraṃ, anantarassa bhāvo ~aṃ); Sadd 891,.25 (atha iti … ~e: atha naṃ āha); — ifc see citt’- sv citta1.

achatta:
1chatta
chatra n. (nom.pl. ~āni, ~ā) [S. chattra], a parasol, a sunshade; an umbrella; a parasol erected on a thūpa; Abh 357; 1130; Vin I 152,.35 (bhikkhū ~e vassaṃ upagacchanti); II 131,.6 (na bhikkhave ~aṃ dhāretabbaṃ); IV 200,.11 (tīṇi ~āni setacchattaṃ kilañjacchattaṃ paṇṇacchattaṃ maṇḍalabaddhaṃ salākabaddhaṃ); Ja III 329,10* (khaggaṃ ~aṃ ca pātiṃ ca gacch’ ev’ ādāya māṇava); IV 55,2* (~aṃ mahantaṃ viya vassakāle); Ap 3,.15 (~ā tiṭṭhantu ratanā, Be, Ce so; Se chattātichattā tiṭṭhanti; Ee suvaṇṇajālābhi saṃyuttaṃ; Ap-a 108,.21 foll. : ~ā tiṭṭhantu ratanā ti ādiṃ āha, tattha ratanā sattaratanamayā ~ā); 170,.22 (pupphacchadanaṃ katvāna ~amhi abhiropayiṃ); 369,.31 (yo me ~am adhāresi pasanno sehi pāṇihi); 405,.4 (paṇḍaraṃ ~am ādāya addhānaṃ patipajj’ ahaṃ); 536,.5 (Sineruṃ daṇḍaṃ katvāna ~aṃ katvā mahāmahiṃ); Mil 415,.27 (~aṃ vātātapameghavuṭṭhiyo paṭihanati); Sp 545,.7 (cetiyassa vā upari bandhissāmi ~aṃ); 894,.30 (yaṃ pi tattha jātakadaṇḍakena kataṃ ekapaṇṇacchattaṃ hoti taṃ pi ~am eva); — a parasol as a sign of sovereignty; esp. as part of the regalia of a king; chattaṃ ussāpetuṃ, to raise the royal parasol (equivalent to “crown” or “be crowned”); the parasol as the symbol of the royal power (“the crown”, “the throne”); D II 15,.9 (dhammatā esā … sampatijāto bodhisatto … sattapadavītihārena gacchati setamhi ~e anuhīramāne); S I 226,.16 foll. (Vepacitti asurindo … khaggaṃ olaggetvā ~ena dhāriyamānena … Sakko devānam indo … khaggaṃ aññesaṃ datvā ~aṃ apanāmetvā … assamaṃ pavisitvā); Sn 688 (anekasākhaṃ ca sahassamaṇḍalaṃ ~aṃ marū dhārayum antalikkhe); Ja IV 125,.18 (Bharatakumāro mama bhātaraṃ Rāmapaṇḍitaṃ araññā ānetvā ~aṃ ussāpessāmī ti); V 264,24* (nikkhippa pañca kakudhāni kāsīnaṃ raṭṭhavaḍḍhano vāḷavījanim uṇhīsaṃ khaggaṃ ~aṃ c’ upāhanaṃ); 322,10* (kassa paggahitaṃ ~aṃ sasalākaṃ manoramaṃ ādiccaraṃsāvaraṇaṃ); VI 31,.11 (~aṃ vā me detha yuddhaṃ vā ti); 470,31´ (taṃ rājānaṃ visena māretvā brāhmaṇassa ~aṃ ussāpetvā); Cp 3:6:4 (addasaṃ paṇḍaraṃ ~aṃ yenāhaṃ nirayaṃ gato); 3:6:14 (veṭhetvā rājaveṭhanaṃ ~ena abhisiñcitvā kāresuṃ purapadakkhiṇaṃ; Cp-a 223,.18 : setacchattena dhāriyamānena); Sp 75,.7 (Asoko … pañca rājakakudha-bhaṇḍāni pahiṇi ~aṃ cāmaraṃ …); Sv 612,.29 (anāgate Piyadāso nāma kumāro ~aṃ ussāpetvā Asoko dhammarājā bhavissati); Spk I 295,.20 (rājaputto ~aṃ pahāya pabbajito); Mp II 239,.13 (rājā cintesi putto me vayappatto ~aṃ assa ussāpetvā rajjasiriṃ passissāmī ti); Cp-a 221,.9 (tayo antarāyā paññāyanti jīvitassa vā ~assa vā mahesiyā vā); Mhv 33:40 (°’-atthāya visajjesuṃ lekhaṃ bhūpatisantikaṃ); Sadd 870,.20 foll. (~aṃ … [garūnaṃ] mate chatraṃ …); — ifc see eka-, kilañja-, cetiya-, dhura-, seta-; —      ° âtichatta,        °âdhichatta,   n., a parasol upon a parasol, a double parasol; Ap 170,.20 (~aṃ kāretvā thūpamhi abhiropayiṃ, Be, Ce, Se so; Ee °âdhichattaṃ; Ap-a 439,.21 : chādiyati saṃvariyati ātapādin ti chattaṃ, chattassa atichattaṃ chattassa uparikatachattaṃ ~aṃ, chattassa uparūpari chattan ti attho, Be, Se so; Ce, Ee °âdhichattaṃ); Dhp-a III 439,.13 foll. 1dhamma
m. (and n.) [S., BHS dharma], dhamma denotes (an interpretation of) the essential nature and reality of existence and experience, the way things are: it is descriptive and prescriptive; it denotes also an essential attribute of men or animals; a quality or characteristic; Abh 784 (~o sabhāve pariyattipaññāñāyesu saccappakatīsu puññe ñeyye guṇācārasamādhisū pi nissattatāpattisu kāraṇādo); see also Sv 99,.3 foll., Ps I 17,.16 foll., It-a I 37,.20 foll., Paṭis-a 18,.1 foll., Bv-a 13,.4 foll., As 38,.23 foll. and Sadd 560,.25 foll.; — for Buddhists dhamma is used to denote an interlocking and interdependent assembly of concepts: the true nature of the world of experience, how that world works, and the way to transcend it, as understood by the Buddha; the progressive stages of understanding and nibbāna ; the behaviour, the practice, required to achieve understanding of the way the world of experience works, ie the way to reach arhatship, nibbāna ; the understanding and practice taught by the Buddha, the substance of his teaching, the texts of the Canon, especially the Suttapiṭaka ; all constituents of the world of experience, physical and mental, external and internal, progressively more and more minutely analysed; all constituents of prescribed practice, appropriate and beneficial actions; prescriptions for the members of the saṅgha ; — for people generally dhamma is an interpretation of the essential nature of existence and experience; the way one should act, depending on who one is, to maintain the way things are and should be; duty; right; justice; normative and beneficial actions; — 1.
